correctness.rationale: Every one of 4096 masks is examined. For full-dimensional subsets the code finds every supporting facet using exact Q(phi) cross products and signs, orders its extreme vertices using exact oriented comparisons and checks each convex turn, then computes volume using the oriented determinant divergence identity. The exact table has correct binomial multiplicities, 29 total values, 75 zero-volume four-subsets, 12 zero-volume five-subsets, and no zero-volume subsets with six or more vertices. Structural checks identify all neighbor-ring and antipodal-pair degeneracies. A numerically independent Qhull implementation checked all 4096 masks with maximum absolute error 1.07e-14; numeric evidence supplements rather than proves the exact exhaustive certificate.

originality.rationale: The indexed earlier tetrahedron result covers exactly the 495 four-point subsets and is expressly credited. The all-cardinality spectrum has 29 distinct volumes and new 5-to-12-vertex layers, including a complete probability and expectation polynomial. Newman 2020 covers the general thinning model without the finite icosahedron enumeration; Jacobson 2026 covers a different outer-approximation operation. Public searches and the inspected primary texts reveal no statement implying the complete table. Historical priority is provisional because one published four-point record was available only in synopsis.

value.rationale: Independent vertex thinning is a natural model for finite polyhedral approximation and robustness. The complete 29-volume class law for a Platonic solid gives exact metric statistics for all retention probabilities, extends a previously known tetrahedral slice across all 12 cardinalities, and reveals the geometric sharp affine-spanning threshold and all degenerate configurations. It is a natural complete finite classification, not a parameter cherry-pick or trivial direct evaluation of a single known formula; neither a general higher-dimensional theorem nor external application is claimed.
